In-depth knowledge of cloud infrastructure administration, with hands-on AWS experience across compute, storage, networking, and IAM.
A minimum of 5 years of experience supporting a regulated or compliance-driven environment (e.g., NIST800-171, FedRAMP, HIPAA, PCI-DSS).
Demonstrated experience with Infrastructure as Code tools such as Terraform or CloudFormation, and configuration management tools such as Ansible or Chef.
Experience with identity and access management, network segmentation, encryption, and logging/monitoring controls needed to protect Controlled Unclassified Information.
Demonstrated experience with system hardening, vulnerability management, and remediation of security findings.
Experience in a regulated or federally funded research computing environment.
Experience with CI/CD and automation tools such as GitHub Actions or Jenkins.
A minimum of 5 years of experience administering cloud infrastructure in AWS.

Under the direction of the Director, AI, Cloud & Client Solutions, the Cloud Compliance Engineer applies advanced cloud engineering and security compliance expertise to independently administer and secure federal research compliant enclaves, meeting regulatory and security requirements that evolve over time. Resolves highly complex issues related to protection of Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI), cloud workload onboarding, and regulatory compliance, where the work demands in-depth evaluation of shifting technical, security, and policy factors. Recommends and selects the methods, tools, and controls needed to maintain continuous compliance and keep the environment secure as those requirements change.
Adhere to OIT’s cultural values: Collaboration, Respect, Trust, Transparency, Quality, Inclusiveness, Customer Centricity, and Learning and Growth.
Solutions Architect Associate
May require on call support after hours or on weekends.
Advanced knowledge of federal research grant control frameworks including their security requirements and their practical application to cloud environments.
Advanced knowledge of computer security tools, best practices, and policies, including securing server-based software and cloud workloads.
Ability to create compliance documentation such as System Security Plans (SSPs), Plans of Action and Milestones (POA&Ms), and control assessments.
Interpersonal and communication skills sufficient to work with both technical and non-technical program/compliance personnel.
Demonstrated organizational skills to manage multiple onboarding efforts and competing priorities.
Ability to write clear, concise technical and compliance documentation.
Familiarity with vulnerability scanning and SIEM tools
